rv.q: The play is nostalgic, funny and heart-warming with tear-jerking poignant moments as Damian battles his abuse and desperately seeks friendship, love and security.
It’s a witty approach to taking a memoir from page to stage, but it doesn’t work. The structure feels scatty and episodic, rarely settling long enough to permit any personal or social insight.
This is a great pity because somewhere in this hall of mirrors is an absorbing 75 minute play.

cn.t: Barr's memoir-to-stage adaptation receives mixed reviews, with critics finding touching themes but faulting long-winded exposition and struggles in translating the book's intimacy to theatrical form.
